example-look-at.title: Quaternion Look At
example-look-at.description: A grid of hand-built arrows that all turn to point at an orb as it drifts overhead — like sunflowers tracking the sun. Each aims with math's quat.rotationTo, the shortest rotation from its +Y tip onto the target direction.

example-fibonacci-sphere.title: Fibonacci Sphere
example-fibonacci-sphere.description: Points spread evenly over a sphere with the Fibonacci lattice, built in math's spherical coordinates (spherical.toVec3) — each steps one equal-area band down while turning by the golden angle, so sunflower-like spiral arms emerge. Nudge the twist off φ to shear them into spokes.

example-contains-point.title: OBB3 Contains Point
example-contains-point.description: An outlined oriented box (math's obb3) tumbles through a sparse lattice of fixed sample points. obb3.containsPoint colors each point green inside the box and grey outside. Hide outside points or pause the motion to inspect the result.

example-convex-hull-3d.title: Convex Hull 3D
example-convex-hull-3d.description: A point cloud and its convex hull, computed with math's quickhull3. Cyan and purple connect hull vertices to a translucent faceted shell, preserving depth cues as the cloud rotates. Choose the Stanford bunny, primitives, or random points.

example-convex-hull-2d.title: Convex Hull 2D
example-convex-hull-2d.description: A drifting 2D point cloud with its convex hull recomputed live (math's quickhull2) — points light up as they wander onto the hull.

example-polygon2-decomposition.title: Polygon2 Decomposition
example-polygon2-decomposition.description: Draw a concave polygon and see how math's decomposePolygon2Quick or decomposePolygon2Quality partitions it into convex pieces. The colored border is the original polygon and light lines are the internal cuts. Hover to highlight a piece, or switch between the original shape and the result.

example-polygon2-triangulation.title: Polygon2 Triangulation
example-polygon2-triangulation.description: Draw a polygon and see math's triangulatePolygon2 partition its interior into triangles without adding vertices. The colored border is the original polygon and light lines are the internal cuts. Hover to highlight a triangle, or switch between the original shape and the result.

example-circumcircle.title: Circumcircle
example-circumcircle.description: A triangle that morphs between shapes with its circumcircle recomputed live (math's circumcircle) — watch the circle balloon as the triangle flattens.

example-fabrik-2d.title: FABRIK 2D
example-fabrik-2d.description: A gallery of 2D inverse-kinematics setups solved with math's fabrik2, following the scenarios in Caliko's own demo app. Move the pointer to lead the chain. Every scenario runs the full solver — forward pass, backward pass, pinned base — through free joints, wedge limits, world-space headings, a trunk with branches wired into a Structure2, and a row of chains each reaching a target of its own.

example-fabrik-2d-snek.title: FABRIK 2D Snek
example-fabrik-2d-snek.description: A snake led by the pointer, driven by one half of math's FABRIK solver — fabrik2.forward alone, which snaps the head onto the target and drags the body after it. No backward pass and no pinned base, so it follows rather than solves; per-joint bend limits keep the body reading as a spine. Eat a pellet and the tail grows at the base end.

example-fabrik-3d.title: FABRIK 3D
example-fabrik-3d.description: A gallery of 3D inverse-kinematics setups solved with math's fabrik3, following the scenarios in Caliko's own demo app — the reference implementation behind the FABRIK paper. Switch between free ball joints, cone rotors, global and local hinges with reference-axis limits, and connected chains whose base rides on a bone of another chain, one of them reaching for a target of its own.

example-flow-field.title: Flow Field
example-flow-field.description: Particles advected along an angle field from math's simplex2d noise. Thin warm-white trails reveal the flow, with one particle in sixteen tracing a thicker cyan path.

example-color-wheel.title: Color Wheel
example-color-wheel.description: An HSL colour wheel built with math/color (hsl.toColor). Move the pointer to pick a colour and read its HSL / RGB / hex.

example-ridged-noise-voxel-terrain.title: Ridged Noise Voxel Terrain
example-ridged-noise-voxel-terrain.description: A voxel landscape from math's ridged fBm, with soft neutral face tones and purple summit caps. A culled mesher emits a quad only for exposed solid faces.

example-simplex-4d-looping-noise.title: Simplex 4D Looping Noise
example-simplex-4d-looping-noise.description: A grid of tiles with soft neutral face tones and subtle edges whose heights come from math's simplex4d. The highest tiles turn pink. Two noise axes trace a circle, making the field return exactly to its starting shape with no seam.

example-simplex-2d-noise-terrain.title: Simplex 2D Noise Terrain
example-simplex-2d-noise-terrain.description: A rolling terrain from math's simplex2d noise, drawn as a softly lit neutral surface with fine elevation contours and heavier lines every fourth level. One amber contour tracks a fixed height as the landscape scrolls.

example-quaternion-slerp.title: Quaternion Slerp
example-quaternion-slerp.description: Two boxes interpolate between the same random orientations — one with math's quat.slerp (smooth shortest arc), one lerping euler angles (the wobbly, long-way-round naive approach).

example-spring.title: Spring2 Tail
example-spring.description: A springy tail that chases the pointer — the head springs to the cursor and each bead springs to the one ahead (math's spring2, under-damped so it overshoots and settles).

example-easing.title: Easing
example-easing.description: A small-multiples gallery of math's easing functions - one card per curve, each plotting the function against a linear reference with a dot tracing it at a shared, ping-ponging time.

example-circle-physics.title: Circle Physics
example-circle-physics.description: A cluster of circles held together by its own gravity, solved with substepped XPBD. There are no walls, and the pointer is just a body with no inverse mass, so ploughing through the pack is the same contact solve as everything else.

example-polygon2-signed-distance.title: Polygon2 Signed Distance
example-polygon2-signed-distance.description: A lattice of probes visualizes math's polygon2.signedDistance. Cyan marks inside and white marks outside. Larger probes trace distance contours. Turn on needles to see the direction to polygon2.closestPoint.

example-frustum-culling.title: Frustum Culling
example-frustum-culling.description: Agents patrol an outlined city, each with a camera of its own. Every building and orb is tested with math's frustum.intersectsBox3 and intersectsSphere. Purple fills mark objects seen by any agent, while faint outlines mark unseen objects. Bright camera bounds come from frustum.corners.

example-dual-quaternion-skinning.title: Dual Quaternion Skinning
example-dual-quaternion-skinning.description: The candy wrapper, side by side. Two identical tubes bound to the same two bones and twisted by the same angle, differing only in how the bone transforms are blended. On the left mat4s blended by weighted sum - averaging two rotation matrices is not a rotation, so halfway through a half turn the tube pinches to a thread. On the right the same bones as math's quat2, where lerp then normalize lands back on a rigid transform and the volume survives.
